meta.description: Safe alphanumeric canary tokens for reflected XSS detection. Each probe contains harmless delimiter boundary characters so that verbatim, unencoded reflection in an HTML context is a reliable indicator of a missing output-encoding control.
meta.usage: Inject each probe string into a GET/POST parameter. If the boundary characters appear in the response body without HTML entity encoding, the endpoint is likely vulnerable to reflected XSS.

probes.description: Detects raw < reflection — sufficient for tag injection context
Classic script-tag canary; expects full angle-bracket reflection
Detects unescaped double-quote reflection inside HTML attribute values
Detects unescaped single-quote reflection inside HTML attribute values
Comprehensive boundary canary — checks all six high-risk delimiter characters in one probe
Script-context breakout: attempts to close an existing <script> block
Attribute breakout with event handler injection probe
Semicolon boundary test — useful for JS and CSS injection contexts
Forward-slash probe for path-segment and self-closing tag contexts

encoded_forms.description: HTML entity encodings that indicate SAFE (properly escaped) reflection. If the response contains these encoded forms instead of raw boundary chars, the endpoint is NOT vulnerable.
